{{nihongo|'''Sakaki Shrine'''|坂城神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Sakaki, {{ill|Sakaki, Nagano|Q1348962|qid=Q1348962}}, {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|Q726661|qid=Q726661}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank in the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. {{nihongo|'''Sakaki Shrine'''|坂城神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

== Overview ==
The main deity is {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}. Shrine tradition says that in year 40 of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258}} enshrined his ancestral deity here during the eastern expedition, and in {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} 2 ({{ill|673|Q31105|qid=Q31105}}) shrine buildings were dedicated to pray for good governance and peace under heaven.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=register of deities}} of the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}', completed in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed as "Sakaki Shrine" in {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|Q726661|qid=Q726661}}, {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}}, and ranked as {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

It was worshiped as the village shrine of Sakaki-gō, Hanishina District, and from the medieval period onward was called "Sakaki Ōmiya." It was revered by generations of the {{ill|Murakami clan|Q11522833|qid=Q11522833}}, lords of {{ill|Katsurao Castle|Q11620930|qid=Q11620930}}, and the site includes Mansen-ji, the remains of the Murakami residence, adjacent to the precincts. Katsurao Castle fell to the {{ill|Takeda clan|Q1210114|qid=Q1210114}} in {{ill|Tenbun|ckb|تێنبون|fa|تنبون|fi|Tenbun-kausi|fr|Ère Tenbun|it|Tenbun|ja|天文 (元号)|ko|덴분|pt|Tenbun|ru|Тэмбун|simple|Tenbun|sr|Тенбун|sv|Tenbun|tr|Tenbun|zh|天文 (日本)|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 22 ({{ill|1553|Q6568|qid=Q6568}}), but in {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 11 ({{ill|1568|Q6648|qid=Q6648}}), {{ill|Takeda Shingen|Q276404|qid=Q276404}} donated shrine lands and revived it, and {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|Q662482|qid=Q662482}} also guaranteed those lands in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 7 ({{ill|1579|Q6709|qid=Q6709}}).

It is also said to have been greatly revered by magistrates of the {{ill|Nakanojō Jin'ya|Q21653911|qid=Q21653911}} in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}.

== Cultural properties ==
== Sakaki Town designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible cultural properties
** Wooden Kishin mask (sculpture) - designated October 1, 1984 (Shōwa 59).
** Wooden lion head (sculpture) - designated October 1, 1984 (Shōwa 59).
** One pair of Sakaki Shrine komainu (sculpture) - designated April 1, 1999 (Heisei 11).
** Four old documents of Sakaki Shrine (old documents) - donation letter of shrine lands by Takeda Shingen, guarantee letter by Takeda Katsuyori, prohibition by Hasegawa Yasazaemon, donation letter of sacred lands by Murakami Yoshikiyo. Designated October 1, 1984 (Shōwa 59).
